GitHub Issue:
Post Date: 2018-08-23T09:15:45Z
Current Date: April 4 2025
Title: Give Flowable.sequenceEqual()/BiPredicate the option to use Single<Boolean> instead of boolean
Description: I need to compare two `Flowable`s, that unfortunaley, due to `groupBy()` do not complete until all items it contains are subscribed to. 

Currently, this is not possible since test() in the BiPredicate you can implement for `sequenceEqual()` can only return a `boolean`, it expects the `Flowable` to be comparable one by one. I suggest to overload `test()` so that it can also return `Single<Boolean>` - thus allowing the comparison to happen for all elements of the `Flowable` before expecting it to complete, which lets every item be subscribed to.

This is a feature request that involves API design and functionality enhancement, not a bug that needs to be reproduced to verify a solution. The issue describes a limitation in the current API where the BiPredicate's test() method can only return a boolean, making it difficult to compare Flowables that don't complete until all items are subscribed to. Understanding and evaluating this request requires knowledge of RxJava's API design and reactive programming concepts, but doesn't require actually building and running code to verify. A solution to this issue would be a code change proposal that can be evaluated by reviewing the API design, not by running tests that require a build environment.
